claimBoundary: V18 localizes why V15 and V16 differ. It can distinguish structural-control failure from loss of statistical support, but it does not establish translation, semantic identity, historical contact, common authorship, theological identity, phonetic equivalence, causal mechanism, or machine execution.

boundary.description: remove START-padded and END positions; retain only current positions with four real predecessors and a real successor

frequency.description: restrict candidate pairing to operators within 0.15 train frequency percentile, changing no event count

proper.description: exclude Hebrew candidate lemmas with any proper-noun-tagged train occurrence, changing no event count

seenNew.description: collapse SEEN_EARLIER_SEGMENT and NEW_SEGMENT to OTHER, changing no event count

segment.description: restrict to 6–10 item segments and at most three deterministic eligible events per segment

volumeSham.description: retain the V15 projector but deterministically thin its event set to exactly the event count produced by the named structural control in that corpus/lane

hebrewSource.properNameMask: OSHB morphology is recorded only so the proper-name control can exclude train lemmas; baseline V15 machinery ignores morphology
hebrewSource.tokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>

interpretation.cumulativeRule: cumulative rungs are diagnostic only; no semantic claim is made from them
interpretation.nonvolumeRule: seenNew, proper, or frequency is an isolated breaker only if exact baseline passes and the exact-V15 isolated variant is train-feasible but fails two-lane V15 gates
interpretation.thinningRule: boundary or segment is a structural breaker only if its exact-V15 variant fails while the corresponding event-count-matched V15 sham remains feasible/passing; if both collapse, classify support thinning as confounded/sufficient to explain loss of analyzability

question: Which V16 stress controls break the V15 correspondence when the V15 fitting, support, pairing, null, and gate machinery is held exact?
